reports.title: Hyperliquid Strategies Inc Reports Financial Results

desk.headline: Net income of $620.6m, driven by an $803m paper gain on HYPE tokens; HYPE holdings up to 38.5m; no guidance given

other.label: Unrealised gain on HYPE tokens
other.change: HYPE price $65.04 to $90.99 in the quarter

results: Revenue from staking and validator fees was $12.3m (labelled 'revenue' by the company), plus $1.0m of interest; costs were $7.6m.
Net income of $620.6m came almost entirely from an $803m unrealised gain as the HYPE token price rose; it is not cash profit.
The company raised $911m by selling new shares and spent $785m buying 9.1m HYPE tokens, while also buying back 2.7m of its own shares for $17m.
Net asset value rose 82% to $3.4bn; tokens worth $3.5bn make up about 93% of assets. No debt.
A subsidiary applied to become a futures commission merchant, aiming to serve US clients on regulated Hyperliquid markets, subject to approval.

guidance.summary: The company gives no financial guidance; results mainly track the price of the HYPE token.

points: Management framed buying HYPE and the broker-licence application as one bet on Hyperliquid's fee growth.
About 99% of Hyperliquid's fees go to buying back HYPE tokens automatically, which the company likens to a share buyback.
The company sells new shares when its market value is above net asset value and buys back shares when it is below.
Regulated US access to Hyperliquid markets is presented as the next big opportunity, but still needs regulatory approval.
call.source: Earnings presentation (Exhibit 99.2) and CEO comment in the press release; no call coverage found

watch: The HYPE token price, which drives the company's reported profit and asset value.
Progress on the futures commission merchant application and US regulated markets.
Pace of new share issuance versus buybacks, and the share price relative to net asset value.
